reason: The passage depicts the early narrative of Moses in Egypt, where individual Hebrews are portrayed as enslaved laborers (סִבְלֹתָם - their burdens/labors) under Egyptian oppression. The events described are personal confrontations—Moses witnessing an Egyptian striking a Hebrew laborer and Moses individually killing the Egyptian—rather than a collective national political struggle. Critically, the action takes place in Egypt, not on Hebrew land, and there is no portrayal of an organized national movement for political liberty. The Hebrews appear as oppressed individuals subject to Egyptian authority, not as a nation engaged in political resistance for freedom on their own territory.
